items.title: Prometheus Platform
items.text: Welcome to the Prometheus documentation. This site serves as the central reference for Prometheus' projects' architecture, usage, and development.

items.title: What is Prometheus?
items.text: Prometheus is one of the Genesis' challenges for the "Delivering Nuclear Energy That is Faster, Safer, Cheaper" challenge

items.title: Documentation
items.text:
• Platform -- FastAPI backend + Chainlit frontend for workflow orchestration
  • API -- StorageClient and PrometheusAgent Python toolkit
  • Agent Template -- Scaffolding tool for creating new A2A agents
  • Contributing -- How to set up your local environment, write docs, and use the available markdown features

items.title: Contributing to Prometheus Docs
items.text: This guide covers how to set up your local environment, write and preview docs, and use the available markdown features.

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
• Python 3.12+
  • uv package manager

items.title: Local Development
items.text:
# Install dependencies
uv sync

# Start the local dev server with hot-reload
uv run zensical serve

# Build the site for production
uv run zensical build --clean

The dev server watches for changes in docs/ and reloads automatically. The production build outputs static HTML to site/.

items.title: Project Structure
items.text:
docs/           # Markdown source files — all content goes here
site/           # Generated output (do not edit)
zensical.toml   # Site configuration (theme, features, palettes)

items.title: Adding a New Page
items.text:
1. Create a new .md file in the docs/ directory
  2. Add frontmatter at the top with an icon (optional): 
    ---
icon: lucide/file-text
---
  3. Preview locally with uv run zensical serve

items.title: Deployment
items.text: Pushing to main triggers the GitHub Actions workflow which builds and deploys to GitHub Pages automatically. No manual deployment is needed.

items.title: Writing Style
items.text:
• Use sentence case for headings
  • Keep pages focused on a single topic
  • Link to the Zensical docs for feature details rather than duplicating their documentation

items.title: Math (MathJax)
items.text:
MathJax is not enabled globally. To use math on a page, add this script tag at the bottom:

<script id="MathJax-script" async
  src="https://unpkg.com/mathjax@3/es5/tex-mml-chtml.js"></script>

Then use $$ blocks for display math or \( / \) for inline math.

items.title: Prometheus Agent Template
items.text: An interactive scaffolding tool that generates a ready-to-run A2A agent from a template. Run the setup script, answer a few prompts, and get a complete agent with Dockerfile, configuration, and authentication.

items.title: Quick start
items.text:
cd prometheus_agent_template

# Run the scaffolding script
python setup_agent.py

The script prompts for:

Prompt Example Default Agent name Plant Analysis (required) Description Analyzes plant thermal output -- Slug plant-analysis derived from name Class name PlantAnalysis derived from name Skill ID analyze_plant derived from name Skill name Analyze Plant derived from name Skill description Runs plant thermal analysis -- Trim comments? y/n n

After confirmation, it creates a new directory with all files ready to go.

items.title: Run the generated agent
items.text:
cd <output-directory>
cp .env.example .env          # edit with your settings
pip install -r requirements.txt
python agent.py

Or with Docker:

docker build -t my-agent .
docker run -p 8000:8000 --env-file .env my-agent

items.title: Generated files
items.text:
The template produces these files:

File Purpose agent.py Agent implementation -- subclass of PrometheusAgent with process_analysis() to customize agent_card.json A2A agent metadata (name, description, skills, capabilities) .env.example Environment variable template Dockerfile Container config with health check, CA cert support, proxy support requirements.txt Python dependencies (a2a-sdk, pydantic, httpx, uvicorn, prometheus-api[agent]) pyproject.toml Package metadata README.md Agent-specific documentation .python-version Pinned to 3.12

items.title: Template placeholders
items.text:
The setup script replaces these tokens across all files:

Placeholder Replaced with TEMPLATE_NAME Agent name TEMPLATE_DESCRIPTION Agent description TEMPLATE_SLUG Kebab-case identifier TEMPLATE_CLASS PascalCase class name TEMPLATE_SKILL_ID Snake-case skill ID TEMPLATE_SKILL_NAME Skill display name TEMPLATE_SKILL_DESCRIPTION Skill description

items.title: Override process_analysis
items.text:
The only method you need to implement:

from prometheus_api.agent import PrometheusAgent

class MyAgent(PrometheusAgent):
    async def process_analysis(self, params, context, event_queue):
        input_data = params.get("input_data")
        if not input_data:
            raise ValueError("input_data is required")

        # Your logic here
        result = do_analysis(input_data)

        return {"status": "success", "result": result}

items.title: Send progress updates
items.text:
For long-running tasks:

from prometheus_api.agent import (
    TaskState, TaskStatus, TaskStatusUpdateEvent,
)

async def process_analysis(self, params, context, event_queue):
    await event_queue.enqueue_event(
        TaskStatusUpdateEvent(
            taskId=context.task_id,
            contextId=context.context_id,
            final=False,
            status=TaskStatus(state=TaskState.working),
        )
    )
    # ... continue processing

items.text:
Edit agent_card.json to register additional skills:

{

items.title: Use the StorageClient
items.text:
Agents can interact with the storage backend:

from prometheus_api.storage_client import StorageClient, ConnectionConfig, ItemCreate

class MyAgent(PrometheusAgent):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__("My Agent")
        self.storage_config = ConnectionConfig.from_env()

    async def process_analysis(self, params, context, event_queue):
        with StorageClient(self.storage_config) as client:
            item = client.items.create(ItemCreate(
                name="Analysis Result",
                properties=params
            ))
        return {"item_id": item.id}

items.title: Environment variables
items.text:
Variable Required Default Description AGENT_PORT No 8000 Port to listen on AGENT_HOST No localhost Hostname for agent card URL AGENT_SECRET Prod -- Shared secret for Bearer token auth AGENT_SECRET_REQUIRED No false Enforce authentication REGISTRY_URL No -- Agent registry URL for auto-registration DEEPLYNX_KEY If using storage -- API key for DeepLynx DEEPLYNX_SECRET If using storage -- API secret for DeepLynx DEEPLYNX_ORG_ID If using storage -- Organization ID DEEPLYNX_PROJECT_ID If using storage -- Project ID

See .env.example for the full list including proxy and SSL settings.

items.title: Docker deployment
items.text:
The generated Dockerfile:

  • Base image: python:3.11-slim
  • Installs CA certificates and handles custom cert bundles
  • Supports HTTP_PROXY / HTTPS_PROXY build args
  • Health check on /health endpoint every 30 seconds

items.title: Docker Compose (multi-agent)
items.text:
services:
  agent-one:
    build: ./agent-one
    ports:
      - "8300:8000"
    env_file: ./agent-one/.env
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "curl", "-f", "http://localhost:8000/health"]
      interval: 30s
      retries: 3

  agent-two:
    build: ./agent-two
    ports:
      - "8301:8000"
    env_file: ./agent-two/.env

items.title: Agent endpoints
items.text:
Every generated agent exposes:

Path Auth Description GET /health No Health check GET /.well-known/agent.json No Agent card (A2A discovery) POST /message Yes A2A JSON-RPC 2.0 message endpoint

items.title: A2A protocol
items.text:
Agents communicate using JSON-RPC 2.0 with the message/send method:

Request:

{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "method": "message/send",
  "id": "req-1",
  "params": {
    "message": {
      "messageId": "msg-1",
      "role": "user",
      "parts": [{"text": "{\"input_data\": \"value\"}"}]
    }
  }
}

Response:

{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": "req-1",
  "result": {
    "history": [
      {
        "role": "agent",
        "parts": [{"text": "{\"status\": \"success\"}"}]
      }
    ]
  }
}

items.title: Prometheus API
items.text:
A Python toolkit that provides two main components:

  1. StorageClient -- full-featured client for storage operations (sync and async) backed by DeepLynx
  2. PrometheusAgent -- base class for building A2A-enabled agents with minimal boilerplate

items.title: Installation
items.text:
# Basic (StorageClient only)
pip install git+https://github.inl.gov/genesis/prometheus_api.git

# With agent support
pip install "git+https://github.inl.gov/genesis/prometheus_api.git#egg=prometheus-api[agent]"

# Editable / development
git clone https://github.inl.gov/genesis/prometheus_api.git
cd prometheus_api
pip install -e ".[dev]"

items.title: Dependencies
items.text:
CoreAgent extraDev extra
  • httpx>=0.24.0
  • pydantic>=2.0.0
  • python-dateutil>=2.8.0
  • python-dotenv>=1.0.0
  • starlette>=0.27.0
  • uvicorn[standard]>=0.27.0
  • a2a-sdk[http-server]>=0.3.0
  • pytest, pytest-asyncio, pytest-cov
  • black, mypy, ruff

items.title: Configuration
items.text:
Create a .env file (see .env.example in the repo):

# Authentication -- choose one method
# Method 1: API key pair (recommended)
DEEPLYNX_KEY=your-api-key
DEEPLYNX_SECRET=your-api-secret

# Method 2: JWT token
# DEEPLYNX_JWT_TOKEN=your-jwt-token

# Required
DEEPLYNX_ORG_ID=123
DEEPLYNX_PROJECT_ID=456

# Optional
DEEPLYNX_DATA_SOURCE_ID=789
DEEPLYNX_BASE_URL=https://deeplynx.inl.gov/api/v1
DEEPLYNX_TIMEOUT=30.0
DEEPLYNX_MAX_RETRIES=3
DEEPLYNX_VERIFY_SSL=true

Load it:

from prometheus_api.storage_client import ConnectionConfig

config = ConnectionConfig.from_env()  # reads .env automatically

Or configure manually:

config = ConnectionConfig(
    organization_id=123,
    project_id=456,
    api_key="your-api-key",
    api_secret="your-api-secret",
)

items.title: Synchronous usage
items.text:
from prometheus_api.storage_client import StorageClient, ItemCreate, ItemUpdate
from pathlib import Path

config = ConnectionConfig.from_env()

with StorageClient(config) as client:
    # Items
    item = client.items.create(ItemCreate(
        name="Experiment A",
        properties={"status": "active", "priority": 5}
    ))
    item = client.items.get(item_id=item.id)
    client.items.update(item.id, ItemUpdate(name="Experiment A (revised)"))
    client.items.delete(item.id)

    # Pagination
    page = client.items.list(page=1, page_size=100)
    for item in client.items.iter_all(page_size=50):
        print(item.name)

    # Bulk operations
    items = client.items.bulk_create([
        ItemCreate(name=f"Item {i}") for i in range(100)
    ])

    # Tags
    client.items.add_tags(item_id=1, tags=["reviewed"])
    client.items.remove_tags(item_id=1, tags=["draft"])

    # Files
    meta = client.files.upload(Path("data.csv"), description="Results")
    client.files.upload_chunked(Path("large.zip"), chunk_size=10*1024*1024)
    client.files.download(file_id=meta.id, output_path=Path("out.csv"))

    # Relationships
    from prometheus_api.storage_client import RelationshipCreate
    client.relationships.create(RelationshipCreate(
        from_item_id=1, to_item_id=2,
        relationship_type="depends_on"
    ))
    rels = client.relationships.get_item_relationships(
        item_id=1, direction="outgoing"
    )

    # Search
    results = client.search.query("experiment data")
    results = client.search.by_tags(["reviewed"])
    results = client.search.advanced_query({
        "properties.status": "active"
    })

    # Timeseries
    client.timeseries.upload(Path("sensor.csv"), data_source_id=456)
    client.timeseries.query(
        data_source_id=456,
        sql_query="SELECT * FROM sensor_data WHERE timestamp > '2024-01-01'"
    )

items.title: Asynchronous usage
items.text:
import asyncio
from prometheus_api.storage_client import AsyncStorageClient, ConnectionConfig, ItemCreate

config = ConnectionConfig.from_env()

async def main():
    async with AsyncStorageClient(config) as client:
        item = await client.items.create(ItemCreate(name="Test"))

        async for item in client.items.iter_all(page_size=50):
            print(item.name)

        # Concurrent operations
        results = await asyncio.gather(
            client.search.query("test"),
            client.items.list(),
        )

asyncio.run(main())

items.title: Error handling
items.text:
from prometheus_api.storage_client import (
    StorageClientError,   # base
    AuthenticationError,  # 401
    ItemNotFoundError,    # 404 (has .item_id)
    ValidationError,      # 4xx (has .details)
    APIError,             # other (has .status_code, .response_data)
)

try:
    client.items.get(item_id=999)
except ItemNotFoundError as e:
    print(f"Item {e.item_id} not found")
except AuthenticationError:
    print("Invalid credentials")

items.title: PrometheusAgent
items.text: Base class that handles A2A protocol boilerplate. You override one method -- process_analysis -- and call run().

items.title: Minimal example
items.text:
from prometheus_api.agent import PrometheusAgent

class MyAgent(PrometheusAgent):
    async def process_analysis(self, params, context, event_queue):
        data = params.get("input_data")
        return {"status": "success", "result": data}

if __name__ == "__main__":
    agent = MyAgent(agent_name="My Agent")
    agent.run()

Each agent needs an agent_card.json alongside the script:

{
  "name": "My Agent",
  "description": "What this agent does",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "capabilities": {
    "streaming": false,
    "pushNotifications": false
  },
  "skills": [
    {
      "id": "process_analysis",
      "name": "Process Analysis",
      "description": "Analyzes input data",
      "tags": ["analysis"]
    }
  ],
  "defaultInputModes": ["text"],
  "defaultOutputModes": ["text"]
}

items.text:

AGENT_PORT=8000

# Authentication

items.title: Progress updates
items.text:
For long-running tasks, send status updates to the client:

from prometheus_api.agent import (
    PrometheusAgent, EventQueue, RequestContext,
    TaskState, TaskStatus, TaskStatusUpdateEvent,
)

class LongRunningAgent(PrometheusAgent):
    async def process_analysis(self, params, context, event_queue):
        # Notify: working
        await event_queue.enqueue_event(
            TaskStatusUpdateEvent(
                taskId=context.task_id,
                contextId=context.context_id,
                final=False,
                status=TaskStatus(state=TaskState.working),
            )
        )

        result = await self.do_heavy_work(params)
        return {"status": "success", "result": result}

items.title: Using StorageClient inside an agent
items.text:
from prometheus_api.agent import PrometheusAgent
from prometheus_api.storage_client import StorageClient, ConnectionConfig, ItemCreate

class StorageAgent(PrometheusAgent):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__("Storage Agent")
        self.storage_config = ConnectionConfig.from_env()

    async def process_analysis(self, params, context, event_queue):
        with StorageClient(self.storage_config) as client:
            item = client.items.create(ItemCreate(
                name=params.get("name", "Unknown"),
                properties=params
            ))
        return {"status": "success", "item_id": item.id}

items.title: Built-in endpoints
items.text:
Every agent automatically exposes:

Path Description /health Health check (exempt from auth) /.well-known/agent.json Agent card (exempt from auth) /message A2A message endpoint (JSON-RPC 2.0)

items.title: Agent lifecycle
items.text:
When agent.run() is called:

  1. Loads agent_card.json from disk
  2. Creates an executor wrapping process_analysis()
  3. Sets up a Starlette HTTP server with the A2A SDK
  4. Adds health endpoint and Bearer token middleware (if AGENT_SECRET is set)
  5. Registers with the agent registry (if REGISTRY_URL is set)
  6. Starts uvicorn

items.title: Prometheus Platform
items.text: The main application -- a FastAPI backend and Chainlit frontend that together provide a chat-driven interface for triggering and monitoring engineering workflows.

items.title: Architecture
items.text:
graph LR
  U[User] --> F[Chainlit Frontend]
  F -->|POST /api/chat| B[FastAPI Backend]
  B -->|chat response| F
  B -->|workflow response| F
  F -->|stream /api/demo/workflow/run| B
  B -->|NDJSON events| F
  B --> DB[(SQLite)]

The two services run independently and communicate over HTTP. The frontend resolves the backend URL from its config.yml (platform-url key).

Service Directory Port Stack Backend prometheus_platform/backend/ 8001 FastAPI, aiosqlite, uvicorn Frontend prometheus_platform/frontend/ default Chainlit, VTK, pyyaml

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
• Python 3.12+
  • uv package manager

items.title: Install and run
items.text:
# Install dependencies
cd prometheus_platform/backend && uv sync --group dev
cd ../frontend && uv sync --group dev

# Terminal 1 -- start the backend
cd prometheus_platform/backend
make run        # FastAPI dev server on :8001

# Terminal 2 -- start the frontend
cd prometheus_platform/frontend
make run        # Chainlit UI

Log in with admin / admin.

items.title: Common commands
items.text:
All commands run from within backend/ or frontend/:

make run        # Start the service
make test       # Run pytest
make lint       # Ruff linter (report only)
make format     # Ruff formatter check
make fix        # Auto-fix lint + format
make check      # All checks (lint + format + typecheck via mypy)

Run a single test:

uv run pytest tests/test_chat.py       # By file
uv run pytest -k test_name             # By name

items.title: Configuration
items.text:
The frontend reads frontend/config.yml:

chat-intro: "Welcome to the Prometheus Platform."
chat-suggestion-title: "What would you like to do today?"

workflow-suggestions:
  - "I want to design a reactor primary coolant system."
  - "Run FTL Safety Analysis"

local-users:
  - username: "admin"
    password: "admin"
    role: "admin"

platform-url: "http://127.0.0.1:8001"
debug: true
auto-approve-steps: true

agent-names:
  - "MOOSE"
  - "Alchemy"
  - "AutoDONE"
  - "FTL"

Override the config path with PROMETHEUS_CONFIG_PATH=/path/to/config.yml.

items.title: Chat
items.text:
Method Path Description POST /api/chat Send a message. Returns a chat or workflow response type.

Request body:

{
  "message": "string",
  "user_id": "string",
  "session_id": "optional string",
  "context": {},
  "files": []
}

If the message matches a workflow suggestion from config.yml, the response includes workflow_id and workflow_type. Otherwise it returns a plain chat reply.

items.title: Sessions
items.text: Method Path Description GET /api/sessions/{session_id} Session metadata GET /api/sessions/{session_id}/messages Messages in a session (chronological) GET /api/sessions/{session_id}/workflow-steps Workflow steps in a session GET /api/sessions/user/{user_id} All sessions for a user (newest first)

items.title: Demo content
items.text: Method Path Description GET /demo/autodone AutoDONE dynamic form definition GET /demo/ifc Sample IFC building model GET /demo/exodus Sample Exodus mesh file GET /demo/ecar Sample ECAR PDF report

items.title: Workflow streaming
items.text:
Method Path Description POST /api/demo/workflow/run Execute the demo workflow, streaming NDJSON events

Events are streamed line-by-line as JSON objects with event_type:

  • workflow_start -- total step count
  • step_start -- step name, agent
  • step_complete -- response text, optional artifact_url
  • workflow_complete -- final event

items.title: Chat flow
items.text:
1. User sends a message in the Chainlit UI
  2. Frontend POSTs to /api/chat
  3. Backend checks if the message matches a workflow trigger
  4. Returns either chat (displayed directly) or workflow (triggers streaming)

items.title: Workflow execution
items.text:
1. Frontend initiates a stream to /api/demo/workflow/run
  2. Backend executes 5 predefined steps sequentially, each with a simulated delay:
    • Planning (Orchestrator) -- creates the workflow plan
    • Requirements (Requirements Agent) -- generates system requirements
    • Architecture (Systems Architecture Agent) -- extracts system functions
    • 3D model (Alchemy Agent) -- generates an IFC model (artifact: /demo/ifc)
    • ECAR report (ECAR Agent) -- generates a PDF report (artifact: /demo/ecar)
  3. Frontend renders each step as a cl.Step and fetches artifacts at completion

items.title: File upload
items.text:
The frontend detects file type on upload and processes locally:

  • .e / .exo (Exodus) -- VTK processing, rendered with ExodusViewer
  • .ifc -- copied to public/ifc-data/, rendered with IFCViewer
  • .pdf -- displayed inline

items.title: Database
items.text: SQLite via aiosqlite at backend/data/prometheus.db (auto-created on startup).

items.text:
sessions

Column Type Notes id TEXT Primary key user_id TEXT Indexed created_at TEXT ISO 8601 UTC updated_at TEXT ISO 8601 UTC

Column Type Notes id TEXT Primary key session_id TEXT FK to sessions role TEXT user or assistant content TEXT response_type TEXT chat or workflow metadata TEXT JSON string created_at TEXT ISO 8601 UTC

There is no migration tool. Delete prometheus.db to reset the schema.

items.title: State repository
items.text:
Persistence uses the repository pattern:

  • state/base.py -- StateRepository abstract base class
  • state/sqlite.py -- SQLiteStateRepository implementation

The repo is initialized during the FastAPI lifespan and stored on app.state.repo. Routers access it via request.app.state.repo.

items.title: Pydantic models
items.text:
Models are split by purpose:

File Contains models/chat.py ChatMessageRequest, ChatResponse, ResponseType enum models/state.py SessionRecord, MessageRecord, WorkflowStepRecord models/dynamic_form.py FormField, DynamicFormProps, field helper functions

items.title: Dynamic forms
items.text: The dynamic_form.py module provides a form definition system used by the frontend's DynamicForm.jsx component. Supported input types: text, textarea, select, checkbox, number, email, password, date, datetime. Helper functions (create_text_field, create_select_field, etc.) simplify field construction.

items.title: Custom React elements
items.text:
Located in frontend/public/elements/, rendered via Chainlit's cl.CustomElement:

Component Purpose DynamicForm.jsx Configurable forms with validation, timeout countdown, help text IFCViewer.jsx 3D building model viewer (ThatOpen engine, THREE.js) ExodusViewer.jsx VTK-based mesh visualization with playback controls and color presets FollowUpSuggestions.jsx Clickable workflow suggestion cards MermaidViewer.jsx Diagram renderer

items.title: Message handler
items.text: components/message_handler.py is the central router for incoming messages. It determines whether to process a file upload locally, forward a text message to the backend, or initiate workflow streaming.

items.title: Settings handler
items.text: components/settings_handler.py configures the Chainlit sidebar with tabs for model selection, agent toggles, and debug features (form testing, file viewer testing).

items.text:
• Line length: 120
  • Linter/formatter: ruff (rules: E, F; E501 ignored)
  • Type checker: mypy
  • Tests: pytest with pytest-asyncio (asyncio_mode = "auto")

items.title: BearerTokenMiddleware
items.text:
Bases: BaseHTTPMiddleware

Middleware to verify Bearer token authentication for A2A requests.

Validates that all incoming requests contain a valid Bearer token in the Authorization header matching a configured secret.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default app

The Starlette application

required secret str

The shared secret for authentication (optional, reads from AGENT_SECRET env var)

None required bool

Whether authentication is required (default: True)

True Example

from starlette.applications import Starlette from agent.middleware import BearerTokenMiddleware

app = Starlette() app.add_middleware(BearerTokenMiddleware, secret="my-secret", required=True)

Environment Variables

AGENT_SECRET: The shared secret for authentication AGENT_SECRET_REQUIRED: Whether to enforce authentication (default: true)

Security Notes
  • Health check (/health) and agent card (/.well-known/agent.json) endpoints are exempt
  • Token values are never logged (only validation status)
  • Returns 401 Unauthorized with JSON-RPC 2.0 error format on failure

items.title: PrometheusAgent
items.text:
Base class for Prometheus A2A agents.

This class handles all the boilerplate: - Loading agent card from JSON - Setting up Bearer token authentication - Registering with the registry - Starting the HTTP server with A2A protocol

To create an agent: 1. Inherit from PrometheusAgent 2. Override process_analysis() method 3. Call run()

Example 
from prometheus_api.agent import PrometheusAgent

class MyAgent(PrometheusAgent):
    def process_analysis(self, params, event_queue):
        # Your logic here
        return {"status": "success"}

if __name__ == "__main__":
    agent = MyAgent(agent_name="My Agent")
    agent.run()

items.title: process_analysis(params, context, event_queue) async
items.text:
Process the analysis request.

OVERRIDE THIS METHOD to implement your agent's logic.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default params Dict[str, Any]

Parameters extracted from the A2A message

required context RequestContext

A2A request context

required event_queue EventQueue

Queue for sending progress updates

required

Returns:

Type Description Dict[str, Any]

Dict containing the analysis results

Example 
async def process_analysis(self, params, context, event_queue):
    input_data = params.get("input_data")

    # Send progress update
    await event_queue.enqueue_event(
        TaskStatusUpdateEvent(
            taskId=context.task_id,
            contextId=context.context_id,
            final=False,
            status=TaskStatus(state=TaskState.working),
        )
    )

    # Your logic here
    result = do_work(input_data)

    return {"status": "success", "result": result}

items.title: AsyncStorageClient
items.text:
Asynchronous client for storage backend operations.

This client provides a high-level async interface for interacting with the storage backend, including CRUD operations for items, file management, relationships, and search functionality.

Example 
config = ConnectionConfig(
    organization_id=123,
    project_id=456,
    api_key="key",
    api_secret="secret"
)

async with AsyncStorageClient(config) as client:
    item = await client.items.create(ItemCreate(name="Test"))
    results = await client.search.query("test")

items.title: from_env(env_file=None, organization_id=None, project_id=None, **kwargs) classmethod
items.text:
Create configuration from environment variables.

Loads credentials from environment variables or a .env file.

Expected environment variables: - DEEPLYNX_KEY: API key for authentication - DEEPLYNX_SECRET: API secret for authentication - DEEPLYNX_ORG_ID: Organization ID (optional if passed as parameter) - DEEPLYNX_PROJECT_ID: Project ID (optional if passed as parameter) - DEEPLYNX_BASE_URL: Base URL (optional) - DEEPLYNX_JWT_TOKEN: JWT token (alternative to API key/secret)

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default env_file Optional[Path]

{}

# Load from .env file in current directory
config = ConnectionConfig.from_env()
